summary: A personal productivity system designed for people living with attention deficits, cognitive overload, or variable energy levels. Instead of treating productivity as a fixed routine, MISU adjusts the experience to your available capacity — select your energy level and the interface adapts its visual language, task recommendations, and focus environment.
galleryDescription: An energy-aware interface with four distinct visual states — each triggering a unique color palette, ambient audio, and curated task set. Desktop runs a bento grid; mobile reorganizes into sectioned navigation. Built to feel like an operating system for your brain.

processSteps.title: Adapt, don't demand
processSteps.description: Recommendations adjust to energy level, task type, estimated duration, and deadline urgency — reducing the cost of deciding what to do next without removing the user's ability to choose otherwise.

processSteps.title: Make the next step visible
processSteps.description: Instead of presenting all tasks as equally actionable, the scoring engine calculates a bounded selection that helps decide where to start. Low energy states also cap the number and total time of suggestions.

processSteps.title: Connect planning to execution
processSteps.description: The weekly planner (powered by Google Gemini API) coexists with the Pomodoro timer, ambient audio, Focus Shield, and a daily checklist — so the user can move from organizing to working in the same space.

processSteps.title: Ship, then iterate
processSteps.description: Started as a personal tool and evolved into a published web app with public repository — authentication via Supabase, cloud sync, demo mode with example tasks, and support for English, Spanish, and Italian.
